name: Saudi Arabia

facts.religion: Sunni Islam about 85%, Shia about 10 to 12%

snapshot: Iranian missiles hit Riyadh and the oil heartland, then the Houthis broke their truce and struck Saudi cities, bringing the war MBS had worked to avoid to his doorstep.
culture: Saudi Arabia is home to Mecca and Medina, Islam's holiest cities, which receive millions of pilgrims each year. Since 2017 it has rapidly opened up: women can drive, cinemas and concerts are allowed, and the kingdom hosts boxing, Formula One and golf. Bedouin traditions of poetry, coffee and hospitality remain strong, as does Najdi architecture.
society: Oil funds the state and most citizens' jobs. Vision 2030 aims to diversify into tourism, entertainment and industry, including the giant NEOM project, though some plans have been scaled back. Dissent is not tolerated, and executions have hit record levels. The kingdom won the right to host the 2034 World Cup.
situation: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's plan for Saudi Arabia, Vision 2030, depends on a bet: that the kingdom can turn itself from an oil state into a hub for tourism, entertainment and business, building futuristic cities in the desert. That bet needs peace. In 2022 MBS secured a truce with the Houthis in Yemen after seven years of war, and in 2023 restored relations with Iran. In 2026, the war he worked to avoid reached his cities anyway.

When the US and Israel struck Iran on 28 February, Iran fired missiles and drones at Riyadh and the oil-rich Eastern Province, targeting refineries and US forces based in the kingdom; the Saudi Formula One Grand Prix was cancelled (Wikipedia). The bigger shock came from the south. In July, the four-year truce with the Houthis collapsed: the group announced a blockade of Saudi shipping in the Red Sea and hit the Aramco refinery in Jizan, and Saudi jets struck back in Yemen (AFP via Aaj). On 8 September the Houthis launched their heaviest attack in years, striking an airbase at Khamis Mushait and oil sites in Abha, Najran and Jizan, wounding 73 people and setting installations ablaze (Reuters via Al-Monitor). With the Strait of Hormuz partly blocked, Saudi Arabia's pipeline to Red Sea ports is one of the few routes for Gulf oil, which is exactly what the Houthis are now threatening.
power: An absolute monarchy with no elected legislature. The king holds supreme power; the crown prince serves as prime minister and runs the government day to day. The appointed Consultative Assembly advises only. Islamic law is the basis of the legal system.
holders: King Salman, 90; Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman.
